speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This applies to any future developments in the Sungei Serangoon area.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I will share some of the reasons for this consideration.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Actually, at the at the beginning of construction, it appears that the site is directly opposite Kingsford Waterbay condo, as well as Cape View HDB Estate, and another condo next to Kingsford Waterbay.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: If you are looking from the condo across the Sungai Serangoon, it is actually much nearer.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And so, some of the feedback given by my residents include noise and dust disamenity.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: In fact, at this beginning, onset of the construction, and when the bus depot is eventually constructed, there will also be noise and dust disamenity, bearing in mind that bus depot operations typically end late in the evening and start early in the morning.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Tan, we are approaching the end of Question Time.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do give the Minister of State some time to reply to you.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Please do indulge me, because these are very important concerns.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The forested area in this eastern bank of the Sungei Serangoon is a nice, forested area grown over the last 20 over years, notwithstanding the Government regarding it as a brownfield site.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, as per my previous appeals and my previous Parliamentary Questions in 2023, this is the only remaining significant track of green spaces on the eastern half of Singapore of such a size, literally from Tampines Road to Pasir Ris Industrial Drive 1 and to Serangoon East Dam.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: By preserving it, we will allow continual connectivity for migratory birds to fly between the Northern Islands and other parts of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: It will also allow the flora and fauna, and even the wildlife that may dwell in these green spaces, including migratory birds in their annual migration journeys between the Northern and Southern Hemispheres as they fly through Singapore —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Tan, are you coming to the question?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are actually at the end of Question Time.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The redevelopment of Paya Lebar Airbase site into a huge Housing and Development Board estate – I believe 800 hectares, 150,000 homes – just next to this area to this area will have significant environmental —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I have given you a lot of leeway.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are actually at the end of Question Time.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I will have to cut you off there and allow the Minister of State to answer to give a short reply.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong: I am sorry, Sir.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I wanted to clarify that I did not say to the Member that it was near the residential sites.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I in fact said that it was not near any sensitive nature areas.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This was also briefed to the Members of Parliament (MPs) back in February 2018 so that MPs are aware of this.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister Indranee, I believe you have a clarification to make.
